newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING STRIKES TO DENY PENGUINS ROAD VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING STRIKES TO DENY PENGUINS ROAD VICTORY.

text.p: John Cullen's power-play goal with 44 seconds left in regulation Friday lifted the Tampa Bay Lightning into a wild 5-5 tie with the Pittsburgh Penguins.

With the Pens' Shawn Antoski serving a high-sticking penalty, Tampa Bay pulled backup goalie Derek Wilkinson for a 6-on-4 advantage. Cullen fed Roman Hamrlik at the left point and skated into the slot. Hamrlik wristed a shot and Cullen tucked the rebound underneath goaltender Ken Wregget.

"The shot landed at my feet and I just slapped it in. It was a good goal, especially versus the old guys I played with," said Cullen, who played with Pittsburgh from 1989 to 1991 and again in the 1994-95 season.
Penguins coach Ed Johnston summed up his team's failure to win on the road.

"We need to do a better job on penalty killing. We can't win a hockey game if we've got penalties all the time," said Johnston. "We were doing what we wanted to do with the 5-4 lead. We deserved more than one point."
Pittsburgh (4-9-1) remained winless on the road at 0-8-1. The Lightning are 6-6-2 on the season.
"We should have got two points but we made stupid mistakes," said Lemieux. "I guess we'll get a few more chances to get our first road victory."
The Penguins' Jaromir Jagr scored twice and Tampa Bay's Dino Ciccarelli posted his 15th career hat trick. They are tied for the league lead with 13 goals apiece.

In Hartford, Brendan Shanahan inspired a noisy reception but was quiet on the ice but teammates Kris Draper and Martin Lapointe picked up the slack as the Detroit Red Wings dominated the Hartford Whalers 4-1.
Draper and Lapointe scored first-period goals and Mike Vernon stopped 14 shots as Detroit outshot Hartford 50-15 in beating them for the 10th time in their last 11 meetings.
Doug Brown and Darren McCarty also tallied for Detroit.

Brendan Shanahan was held without a point in his return to Hartford. Shanahan demanded a trade and was dealt to Detroit a month ago with defenceman Brian Glynn for centre Keith Primeau and defenceman Paul Coffey.
Shanahan was booed every time he touched the puck and drew one of the loudest roars from the Civic Centre crowd when he was checked to the ice by rookie Nolan Pratt.

"It's pretty much what I expected," Shanahan said. "I just ignored (the fans), my mind's on the game. I'll laugh about it later on, but when the game is on, my mind's on the game. It was an important game to me and the team."
In Anaheim, Garry Valk scored twice and Teemu Selanne added a goal and two assists as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim defeated the Los Angeles Kings 7-4, snapping their six-game unbeaten streak.
Valk's tally at 9:06 of the third period extended the Ducks' lead to 6-3 and his empty-netter with 73 seconds left in regulation sealed the victory.
The Kings lost for the first time in four meetings with their Southern California rivals.
In San Jose, Viktor Kozlov had a goal and an assist and Kelly Hrudey stopped 28 shots to lead the San Jose Sharks past the Dallas Stars 3-1.
After starting the season with nine wins in their first 11 games, the Stars have dropped three of their last four.
"Great goaltending and great penalty killing spelled the win for us," said Sharks coach Al Sims.

In Vancouver, Grant Fuhr continued his mastery of the Canucks with 20 saves and Harry York scored the game-winner midway through the third period as the St Louis Blues ended Vancouver's four-game winning streak with a 4-2 victory.
With St Louis protecting a 3-2 lead, Fuhr made a lunging glove save on Russ Courtnall's wrist shot from the right faceoff circle. He went on to his 26th career triumph over Vancouver.
York's power-play tally with 11:48 remaining gave the Blues a 3-1 lead.

In Phoenix, Peter Forsberg had power-play and shorthanded tallies and Keith Jones added his third goal in two games as the Colorado Avalanche used strong special teams play to beat the Phoenix Coyotes 4-1.
The Avalanche improved to 6-0-2 in their last eight games and are 4-0-1 in their last five on the road. Colorado has outscored their opponents 24-9 during their unbeaten streak.
"They showed why they are the Stanley Cup Champions today," said Coyotes coach Don Hay. "They showed us how far we have to go to reach that level. They took advantage of every mistake we made.
